bio: $anteria is a Canadian recording artist whose releases include “BAD FOR YOU,” “PRETTY THINGS,” “VIOLET” and “F4U.” Hear “F4U” on Northern Dial.

6ODEM3 is a francophone recording project built around Nolan Babin, Ulysse Leclerc and Carl-Aubert Langelier. The trio of writers and producers released W.I.P. and SEXES in 2026, with the latter issued in August through Disques Passeport under licence from 6ODEM3 Production.

AHSIA is a Philadelphia-born, Vancouver-raised singer, songwriter, producer, poet and educator. Her music blends R&B, soul, hip-hop and jazz while using sharp lyricism and humour to explore healing, identity and self-reclamation; her 2026 releases include RUNNIN and SO NICE.

Aiza Ntibarikure, known as Aiza, is a Toronto-based singer-songwriter and actress born in Montreal to Burundian parents. Blending R&B and Afro-pop in both English and French, she released her debut album Sovereignty on September 29, 2023. Alongside music she has built an acting career: she plays superhero Sierra Ectoplex in Netflix's Jupiter's Legacy and Maya Bronté on CBC's Workin' Moms, voices Jazzy in the children's series Jeremy and Jazzy, and has had songs placed in series including Tuca & Bertie and Kim's Convenience.

Québec City-born pop singer-songwriter Alicia Moffet broke through by winning the 2013 season of YTV's The Next Star at 15, earning a chance to record a single licensed by Sony Music Canada. She released "Why Do Boys Lie" in 2014 and appeared on La Voix in 2015. After a string of independent singles in 2019, she released her debut album Billie Ave. in June 2020, named after her daughter, followed by Intertwine (2022) and No, I'm Not Crying (2025). Her bilingual catalogue moves between pop, R&B and folk-tinged ballads. In 2023 and 2024 she co-hosted the reality series Occupation Double.

Paris-born, Québec-raised singer-songwriter and actor Aliocha Schneider works in both French and English. His screen debut came in Bon Cop, Bad Cop (2006), followed by roles in Maman est chez le coiffeur (2008), Le Journal d'Aurélie Laflamme (2010) and Closet Monster (2015). Jean Leloup invited him to record with The Last Assassins before Schneider launched his solo music career with the Sorry Eyes EP in 2016, nominated for Best Folk EP at the 2017 GAMIQ Awards. His albums include Eleven Songs (2017), featuring the single "Flash in the Pan," Naked (2020), and the self-titled Aliocha Schneider (2023).

Toronto-based singer-songwriter Allan Rayman pairs a gravelly voice with shadowy alternative R&B, folding in hip-hop, grunge and alternative rock. He broke through with Hotel Allan, self-released in 2015 and issued through Communion Music in 2016, the label co-founded by Mumford & Sons' Ben Lovett. Its follow-up, Roadhouse 01 (2017), built a narrative record around his "Mr. Roadhouse" alter ego. He earned a 2018 JUNO nomination for Breakthrough Artist of the Year. Further albums Harry Hard-on (2018), Christian (2020), Roadhouse 02 (2022) and The All Allan Hour (2024) followed, matched by a deliberately cryptic visual world.

Andre Waithe is a Montreal rapper and producer whose releases include Some Soul Shit Vol. 2. His production credits include music by FIX, SONABOII and Khayden. Hear his collaboration with ROME, “Not The Usual,” on Northern Dial.

Andy Shauf is a Saskatchewan-born singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist known for detailed narrative songs. Born in Estevan and raised in Bienfait before settling in Regina, Shauf played drums in the Christian pop-punk band Captain before going solo, self-releasing early records and signing to Arts & Crafts in Canada and ANTI- internationally in 2015. His breakthrough came with the 2016 concept album The Party, a Polaris Music Prize shortlist finalist on which he played nearly every instrument himself. He followed it with The Neon Skyline (2020), earned multiple Juno nominations, and records with the band Foxwarren. He moved to Toronto in 2016.

Anna Katarina is a Vancouver-based Canadian-American singer-songwriter, multi-instrumentalist and producer. Trained in classical music from childhood, she studied at Selkirk College and Berklee College of Music, and performs on vocals, keys and guitar. Her solo work blends indie pop and rock with folk and soul; her debut solo album arrived in October 2022. She is also one half of the indie-folk duo Rumour Mill, whose work has received US college-radio play and screen placements in American film and TV.

Toronto-area singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Anna Sofia emerged as a teenager writing candid songs about high-school life. She debuted with the single "Meaner Girl" in 2019 at 15, followed by "I Try" and "No Fun" and her debut EP Self Aware Bitch (2020) on Republic Records. Signed to Universal Music Canada, she released the Broken Perfection EP later that year, working with producers Jeff Hazin and Frank Dukes, and earning notice from Wonderland, Complex, American Songwriter and IDOLATOR. Drawing on '70s and '80s radio pop alongside electronica, hip-hop and lo-fi indie rock, she continued with the 2022 EP LET ME OUT I'M FREE! and later singles on Ultra Records.

Anomalie is the project of Montréal keyboardist, composer and producer Nicolas Dupuis, a classically trained pianist with a background in classical and jazz. His EPs Métropole (2017) and Métropole Part II (2018), inspired by his hometown, established his fusion of jazz-funk musicianship with groove-driven electronic production. He followed them with the Bend the Rules EP with Chromeo (2020), Galerie (2022) and Holidays (2023). Performing as Anomalie Live with a four-piece band, he has toured across North America, Europe and Asia and played Red Rocks, the Montreal Jazz Festival and Electric Forest. His early releases were self-released; he signed with Nettwerk in 2022.

Aqyila is a Toronto R&B singer-songwriter born Taahira Aquiyla Duff, an artist of Jamaican descent. Raised on gospel, reggae and R&B, she began uploading covers and originals online before "Vibe for Me (Bob for Me)" took off on TikTok in 2021. She signed with Sony Music Canada. Her debut EP For the Better (2023) featured "Hello," which won the 2024 JUNO Award for Traditional R&B/Soul Recording of the Year. The viral single "Bloom" followed in 2024, and her debut full-length Falling into Place arrived in March 2025.

ARDN is a Burundian-Canadian rapper based in Edmonton, Alberta. He released his debut EP Goodwill in 2018 and followed it with ALIEN in 2020, building a name on introspective, melodic hip-hop. A snippet of "Til The Morning" went viral on TikTok in 2022. He signed to Capitol Records in 2023, releasing his major-label debut single "Plain Jane" that March. He toured across Canada and Europe opening for Isaiah Rashad. His 2025 album Keep Your Eye on the Sparrow earned a Juno Award nomination for Rap Album/EP of the Year at the Juno Awards of 2026.

Arman Ayva is a Montreal-based composer and producer working in jazz-fusion, jazz-funk, ambient and electronic music. Of Armenian heritage, he has been experimenting with music since 2011, blending jazz-funk grooves with electronic textures and folk undertones. His influences include Marcus Miller and Dave Brubeck, and he releases independently through his own channels.

Québec singer-songwriter Arpin Lépine grew up in Saint-Félix-de-Valois, in the Lanaudière region. Blending country, rap and bluegrass with banjo, slide guitar and hip-hop-informed rhythms, he pairs rural storytelling with an unvarnished vocal style. He released the EPs DANS NOTRE COIN and Chance in 2025, followed by his debut solo album Lune Brune in January 2026.

Belize-born, Toronto-raised rapper Asun Eastwood is part of Canada's underground hip-hop scene and a member of the Brown Bag Money collective. Raised on Wu-Tang, he makes sample-driven boom-bap built on vivid storytelling and dense lyricism. His catalogue runs from the 2017 debut mixtape Hollywood Briggs through the Finn-produced With All Due Respect (2019) to collaborations with Futurewave and Daniel Son (Physics of Filth, Bite The Bullet), the Vago-produced Sewer Science (2020), and joint projects with Rochester's MAV and Toronto's Sibbs Roc.

AVIV is a Toronto artist whose independent catalogue moves through alternative pop and singer-songwriter territory. In 2026, she surfaced new material including Mind Candy alongside demos and works in progress shared through her official SoundCloud.

Vancouver rapper Boslen, born Corben Bowen, grew up in Chilliwack, British Columbia, and turned to music full-time after rugby injuries ended his University of Victoria scholarship, dropping out in 2018. That year he released the Motionless and Motionless II mixtapes, finding his sound on 2019's Black Lotus EP. He signed to Capitol Records and issued his debut album DUSK to DAWN in 2021, a cinematic alt-rap record mixing trap rhythms with rock, pop and punk energy and featuring Charmaine, Dro Kenji, Rascalz, Vory and Tyla Yaweh. He followed it with the GONZO EP on June 24, 2022.
Brody Myles is a Canadian recording artist whose EP GONER includes “Did you wrong,” “Toe the line” and “All in.” Hear “Did you wrong” on Northern Dial.

Charmaine Willie, known as Charmaine, is a Zimbabwean-Canadian rapper based in Toronto. Her Warner Music Canada debut single, "Bold" (2020), won the Juno Award for Rap Single of the Year in 2022, the first year the category was presented as a standalone award. She followed it with her debut EP, Hood Avant Garde (2021), featuring "Bold" and "WOO!". Named a Spotify Canada RADAR artist and Amazon Music Canada's Breakthrough artist, Charmaine pairs assertive, high-energy flows with a strong R&B singing voice.

Cherrykim is a Montréal-based recording artist born in South Korea. His recent catalogue includes Can You Feel It?, everynight, Reach Out and the 2026 collaboration Breathe with Vancouver artist Luvinya.

Chikoruss is a Montreal R&B artist whose music draws on the melodies and dance energy of early-2000s R&B. His catalog includes “Body Language,” “In 2 Deep” and “Can't Stop (Loving You),” the latter appearing on R&Bounce Vol. 1.

Colin Léo is a Montréal singer-songwriter who combines hip-hop, pop and R&B with elements of Québec folk and alternative music. A 2026 Francouvertes participant, he released Mêmes habitudes in August, a song built around the repeating-cycle idea of a failing relationship.

Concepcion is the project of Filipino-Canadian R&B singer and songwriter John Concepcion, from Winnipeg. His catalog includes “HITMYLINE,” “Space in Between” and the EP It's Just Luv. Hear “bee's in a garden” on Northern Dial.

Connor Price is a Canadian rapper, actor, and internet personality from Markham, Ontario. He began performing at six and built a long acting career first, appearing as Jay Braddock in the film Cinderella Man (2005), as Kenny on Syfy's Being Human, and as Harry James on CBC's X Company. He turned to hip-hop in the late 2010s, releasing the debut project 4 of Clubs in 2018. In 2022 he released the singles "Spinnin," "Bankroll," and "Buddy," followed by the viral Spin the Globe series, in which he collaborates with an artist from whichever country his finger lands on, released as the Spin the Globe project (2023) and Spin the Globe 2 (2024). His debut studio album About Time arrived in 2025.

CRi is the stage name of Christophe Dubé, a Québec electronic musician and producer. He began as a beatboxer in the electro-hip-hop group Feuilles et Racines before launching his solo electronic project with a self-released EP in 2013. He signed to the UK label Anjunadeep in 2019. His 2020 debut album Juvenile, featuring the Daniel Bélanger collaboration "Signal," blended warm house grooves with French-language songwriting; it earned an Electronic Album of the Year nomination at the 2021 Juno Awards. In 2021 he was named Révélation de l'année (Breakthrough Artist) at ADISQ, and he followed up with the album Miracles (2023), featuring Half Moon Run and Klô Pelgag. His earlier EPs include Tell Her (2016) and Initial (2019); Someone Else (2017) earned a Juno nomination for Electronic Album of the Year in 2018.

Deadly Alfano is the solo project of Toronto singer-songwriter Francesco Alfano, launched after years fronting the Toronto band Lucid Movement. His single "Shelter," released October 2, 2026, was produced by J.C. Sandoval of St. Doval, mixed by Andrew Lauzon at Hamilton's Grant Avenue Studio and mastered by Noah Mintz at Lacquer Channel. Alfano leads the live band on vocals and guitar, joined by Sandoval on bass, Trison Boyes on guitar and Adam Houle on drums.

Dear Rouge are a Vancouver-based husband-and-wife alternative rock duo formed in 2012 by Danielle and Drew McTaggart. Both were touring musicians in other projects (Danielle in the duo Gaetz Ave, Drew in the band Maclean) when they met, married, and started the band, taking its name from Danielle's hometown of Red Deer, Alberta. After winning Vancouver's Peak Performance Project in 2012, their self-released single "I Heard I Had" became a Canadian radio hit and won the SOCAN Songwriting Prize. Following their major-label debut Black to Gold (2015), they won the Juno Award for Breakthrough Group of the Year in 2016. They followed it with PHASES (2018), Spirit (2022) and Lonesome High (2024).
Dee End is a French-language rap artist from Montreal. His releases include Amour Et Trahison and ALTER EGO, alongside tracks “Occupation Hood,” “Mood Gouyad” and “Star 2 Quoi.”

Desiire is a Toronto-based singer-songwriter born in Kinshasa, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, who moved to Scarborough at 12. He began singing in his mid-teens, blending '90s R&B vocals with synth-pop and electronic production. His releases include the Starlight EP (2021). In 2020 he sang on ArtistsCAN's all-star rendition of "Lean on Me" for COVID-19 relief in Canada, alongside Justin Bieber, Bryan Adams, Avril Lavigne and others.

DiRTY RADiO are a Vancouver dance-R&B band formed in 2010 by Farshad "Shadi" Edalat (lead vocals, percussion), Zachary "Waspy" Forbes (DJ, production) and Anthony "Tonez" Dolhai (mixing, production). Fusing progressive pop, R&B and electronic music, their albums include Debut, Cassette and Pleasures, alongside the Lick 1.0 EP and singles including "Numbers," "True Love" and "My Life." Their music has appeared on international labels including Spinnin' Records, Fool's Gold and Mad Decent, and they have shared stages with acts including Dragonette, Funk Hunters and Lights.

dvsn (pronounced "division") are a Toronto R&B duo pairing vocalist Daniel Daley with producer Nineteen85 (Paul Jefferies). After releasing their first songs in 2015, they signed to Drake's OVO Sound label in 2016 and released the debut album Sept. 5th the same year, appearing on Drake's "Faithful" from Views. Their atmospheric slow jams continued on Morning After (2017) and A Muse in Her Feelings (2020), which featured collaborations with PARTYNEXTDOOR, Ty Dolla $ign, Summer Walker, and Jessie Reyez. They teamed with Ty Dolla $ign again for the joint album Cheers to the Best Memories (2021) and released Working on My Karma in 2022.

Etienne Dufresne is a French-language singer and songwriter recording for Duprince Records. His single “pauvre pomme” was written and produced with Benoit Parent, with additional vocals from Lysandre Menard. Hear it on Northern Dial.

frank is a Canadian independent artist whose 2026 releases include bike song, flynn rider, dirt and onions and your biggest fan. The latter was featured by CKMS-FM's Northern Lights program in a September 2026 episode dedicated to new Canadian music.

FRVRFRIDAY is the stage name of Tommy Ruhingubugi, a Rwandan-born Canadian singer, rapper and producer. Born in Rwanda and raised in Montreal from the age of two, he made his first beat on the family computer at 14 and released his debut single "Got It" in 2017, followed by the EPs More Than You Know and Offline and the six-track WHOISFRIDAY. His 2020 single "Window Shopping" featured Lil Baby, and his collaboration with fellow Canadian Anders, "What I Like," earned a nomination for Rap Single of the Year at the 2022 Juno Awards.

Toronto producer and DJ Grandtheft is the recording alias of Aaron Waisglass, whose club-focused electronic music ranges from trap and moombahton to future house, informed by hip-hop, dancehall and bass music. By the early 2010s his career accelerated with releases on Mad Decent, Top Billin and Spinnin' Records, plus a Diplo collaboration remixing Calvin Harris's "Sweet Nothing." His Quit This City EP arrived in 2015 on Mad Decent. His 2014 Keys N Krates collaboration "Keep It 100" won a MuchMusic Video Award and appeared in the Minions movie trailer, and his 2016 single "Easy Go" with Delaney Jane followed.
House Mouse is a Canadian recording artist with “benny and joon” in Northern Dial's rotation.
Jon Rivera is a Canadian recording artist with “Genesis 3:12” in Northern Dial's rotation.

American-born, Toronto-raised singer-songwriter Justin Nozuka built his name on intimate acoustic songwriting, releasing his debut Holly in 2007 after writing its songs as a teenager; Glassnote Records picked it up for its 2008 reissue, and Holly earned him a 2008 JUNO nomination for New Artist of the Year. Follow-up You I Wind Land and Sea (2010) topped Billboard's Heatseekers chart and earned a JUNO nomination for Adult Alternative Album of the Year, while Ulysses (2014) stretched his folk-soul palette further. Later releases, including 2023's Daydreams & Endless Nights, moved him toward lush alternative R&B, and he has performed on The Late Show with David Letterman.

K!RA OJI is a rapper and songwriter who moved from Angoulême, France, to Montreal's South Shore as a teenager. He released the EP Protagoniste with producer DJ Kleancut in 2022, followed by Chercheur de lumières in 2023. Hear his collaboration with Nicky Savage, “BITCHBOYJCONNAISLECODE,” on Northern Dial.

KARABA is a DJ, producer and former professional dancer born in Grenoble, France and raised in Montréal. Her music sits at the intersection of Afro house and underground club music, and her recent work includes the Tides remixes and 2026 singles such as Iya Yemoja, FOCUS, BIG DRIP and LMHYS.

Karim Ouellet (1984–2021) was a Senegalese-born Canadian pop singer-songwriter based in Quebec City. Born in Dakar on December 8, 1984 and adopted by Canadian diplomats, he lived in France, Rwanda and Tunisia before his family settled in Quebec City when he was 15. He released his debut album Plume in 2011, then broke through with Fox (2012) and its hit "L'amour"; Fox won the Juno Award for Francophone Album of the Year in 2014. His third album, Trente, arrived in 2016, the same year as the Aïkido EP. His French-language pop blended folk, soul, reggae and electronic influences.

KAYAM is a Canadian-born singer-songwriter from Calgary whose Tanzanian, Kenyan, Indian and British family background feeds a sound spanning pop, hip-hop, R&B and Afrobeats. His catalogue includes Paralyzed, Ride For Me and Your Soniya, while the 2026 single Singing In The Rain extends his contemporary R&B direction.

Scarborough-born singer-songwriter Kellylee Evans is a Juno Award-winning jazz and soul vocalist. Educated at Carleton University, where she earned degrees in law and English before turning to music full-time, she took second place at the 2004 Thelonious Monk International Jazz Vocals Competition. Her debut album Fight or Flight? (2006) earned a Juno nomination; her Nina Simone tribute Nina (2010) won the 2011 Juno for Vocal Jazz Album of the Year. Come On was released in France in 2015 and earned a 2018 JUNO nomination. After a lightning strike in 2013 and subsequent health setbacks sidelined her for several years, she returned to performing. She has opened for John Legend, Tony Bennett and Erykah Badu.

Kerrington Gillespie is a country-pop singer and songwriter from Vancouver Island. Her releases include “New Boyfriend” and “Three Missed Calls,” with live performances at venues and festivals across British Columbia.

Kimmortal is the professional name of Kim Villagante, a queer Filipino-Canadian musician, singer-songwriter and visual artist based in Vancouver. Raised in Surrey, British Columbia, Kim released a debut album Sincerity in 2014 and broke through with X Marks the Swirl (2019), which was longlisted for the Polaris Music Prize. Their music moves between rap, hip-hop, R&B, soul and experimental sounds, addressing race, gender, identity and community. Their original song "Made Up My Mind" for the series Sort Of won Best Original Song at the Canadian Screen Awards. They have opened for Thundercat, Saul Williams and Ruby Ibarra, and performed at SXSW and Junofest.

Toronto band Kiwi Jr. plays jangly, literate guitar pop drawing on the slacker-pop lineage of the 1980s and 1990s. Formed in 2015, the band is built around Charlottetown, Prince Edward Island transplants Jeremy Gaudet (vocals, guitar), Brian Murphy (guitar), Mike Walker (bass) and Brohan Moore (drums), who moved to Toronto and began playing together. Their debut album Football Money (2019) on Mint Records introduced their wiry, hook-laden sound. They signed to Sub Pop for Cooler Returns (2021) and Chopper (2022), the latter produced by Dan Boeckner of Wolf Parade and Handsome Furs. They released their fourth album, Blowin' Up, in August 2026.

La Sécurité are a Montreal dance-punk group bringing together musicians from the city's indie scene: vocalist Éliane Viens-Synnott, guitarists Melissa Di Menna and Laurence-Anne Charest-Gagné, bassist Félix Bélisle (Choses Sauvages) and drummer Kenny Smith. Their debut album Stay Safe! arrived in 2023 on Mothland and was longlisted for the 2024 Polaris Music Prize. They toured the United States in 2024 supporting The Go! Team, and released the remix EP Stay Safe! REMIXED the same year. Their second album, Bingo!, followed in June 2026 via Bella Union and Mothland.

Laroie is the project of Montreal singer and songwriter Gab Godon, formerly of Heartstreets. The music brings R&B and downtempo production into dancefloor grooves. Releases include the EP Tragedy and “More Than Friends,” now playing on Northern Dial.
